title: Two knights against a bare king and a pawn

D0.outcome: Explains why two knights cannot force mate against a bare king and why a defender's pawn can change that.

D1.outcome: Classifies K+2N against K and K+2N against K+P positions as drawn or won.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, finds the winning approach in the K+2N v K+P cases that win, and recognises the ones that do not.

D3.outcome: Verifies with the tablebase and explains the stalemate geometry.

misconceptions: Two knights always beat a king and pawn.
conditions: Two knights cannot force mate against a bare king; mate can be forced in some positions where the defender has a pawn that can still move.
contrasts: Believing two knights always beat K+P.
The wing where the pawn stands.
